fields.description:
## Symptom

The hourly LaunchAgent `com.navapbc.rebar-dev-update`, which keeps this host's **global**
`rebar` / `rebar-mcp` aligned to `origin/main`, has failed 120+ consecutive times and is
still failing. The global build is pinned at `cdfd7d94dc2fe7671a7eba48e31f36c30f39235c`
(2026-08-28) — 201 commits behind `origin/main` at the latest check, and climbing hourly.
`launchctl list` reports last exit status 1 for the agent.

Every hourly run logs the same rejection:

```
error: Required uv version `==0.12.7` does not match the running version `0.12.9`
candidate ebbcd7a030d6... rejected at sync; current left untouched
candidate-rejection streak now 122 (latest stage: sync)
```

## Root cause

`~/.local/bin/rebar-dev-update.sh:18` hardcodes `UV_BIN` to an absolute Homebrew path and
`:120` orders PATH to keep it authoritative. That premise has INVERTED: Homebrew's uv is now
0.12.9, past the repository's exact `required-version = "==0.12.7"`, while the
`~/.local/bin` standalone sits at 0.12.7. The guard written to stop a stale uv being
selected is now the mechanism selecting one. Substituting the other absolute path
re-inverts the moment that side updates first. Full forensics — the `febd` precedent, the
SNS failure, and the impact measurement — are preserved in the ticket comments.

## The detection gap is the priority half

`REJECT_STREAK_ALERT` (threshold 3) fired every hour and failed to deliver every time: the
IAM principal is in account 820258254566, the SNS topic in 896586841071, and no
resource-based policy permits the cross-account publish. The streak therefore reached 120+
against a threshold of 3 with zero operator signal. Whatever causes the next stall, it is
equally silent unless a detector exists that does not depend on a remote sink.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1 — An on-demand `launchctl kickstart -k gui/$(id -u)/com.navapbc.rebar-dev-update`
  publishes a `current` whose sha equals `origin/main` at that moment. Checked by
  `[ "$(cat ~/.local/state/rebar-dev/current/sha)" = "$(git ls-remote origin main | cut -f1)" ]`,
  by `! grep -q '^error: Required uv version' ~/.local/state/rebar-dev/update.log`, and by
  `[ "$(cat ~/.local/state/rebar-dev/reject-streak)" -eq 0 ]`.
- [ ] AC2 — The updater selects a uv satisfying the CANDIDATE COMMIT's own
  `required-version`, read from that commit's `pyproject.toml` at sync time, rather than any
  hardcoded absolute path. When no available uv satisfies it, the run fails with a message
  naming the required version, each version found, and each path inspected. DISPOSITION of
  that failure is a SOFT RETRY, not a terminal stop: the candidate is rejected at its own
  `uv-select` stage, `current` is left untouched, the streak increments, and the next hourly
  tick retries — matching the existing `rejected at sync; current left untouched` behaviour,
  so a since-fixed or transient pin heals without operator action. Checked by running the
  resolver against a checkout whose pin no local uv satisfies and asserting the message
  names all three facts, and against one whose pin is satisfiable and asserting it selects
  that uv.
- [ ] AC3 — WITHDRAWN by operator decision: the cross-account SNS authorization is not
  being pursued and the sink stays as-is. AC4 absorbs the detection requirement.
- [x] AC4 [non-codebase] — WITHDRAWN from rebar's shipped surface by operator
  decision on Gerrit change 2608, reaffirmed on change 3014. Detection of a stalled updater
  or an over-stale build lives in the LOCAL-ONLY tooling OUTSIDE this repository, not in
  `rebar doctor` and not in `docs/user-guide.md`.

  The original wording required two signals sourced from the host's main-tracking
  LaunchAgent: `reject-streak` (that updater's own counter) and `build-stale` (measured
  against that updater's `current` pointer). Both read `~/.local/state/rebar-dev/`, written
  by a setup described in `docs/local-env-main-tracking.local.md` — a file that is
  git-ignored precisely because it is one operator's machine configuration rather than rebar
  behaviour. Shipping a scan for it would put that configuration into the product and into
  documentation every user reads.

  Two changes implemented this AC as written and both were rejected for it: 2608 (operator
  `Code-Review-1`, abandoned) and 3014 (`LLM-Review-1`, scope-intent, abandoned). The
  rescope promised on 2608 was never written into this description, which is why the second
  attempt reproduced the first one's rejection.

  A GENERAL capability — warn when the installed rebar is far behind `main`, affecting any
  developer with a stale install — remains plausible and is explicitly a SEPARATE FEATURE
  requiring its own ticket. It must reference no machine-local paths. It would not start
  from scratch: `rebar.llm.build_drift.running_build_sha()` already resolves the running
  build's commit, and `BuildDrift` already carries `commits_behind` against a pinned ref.
  That capability is deliberately NOT tracked here.

  Marked `[non-codebase]` because the done-evidence is a decision recorded on Gerrit changes
  2608 and 3014, not an artifact in this repository's tree.
- [ ] AC5 — The pruner's `Directory not empty` failures are resolved and the partial
  release stub `5fb693345b0cd...1559` is reclaimed. Checked by
  `! ls ~/.local/state/rebar-dev/releases | grep -q '^5fb693345b0cd'`, and by
  `! grep -q 'Directory not empty' ~/.local/state/rebar-dev/launchd.err.log` after a
  subsequent run.

## Testing

Repository-side (AC4), from a worktree with `.venv/bin` first on `PATH`:

```
python -m pytest tests/unit/test_doctor_build_freshness.py -q
python -m pytest tests/unit/test_mechanism_delta.py -q
make lint
make typecheck
```

`test_doctor_build_freshness.py` is the named coverage for BOTH AC4 signals, not only
`build-stale`: it asserts the `reject-streak` finding at, above and below its threshold and
on a corrupt counter; the `build-stale` finding above and below its threshold and on a sha
absent from the repo; the absent-state `unavailable` path; and that both reach an operator
through `rebar doctor` in text and JSON without altering its exit code.

Host-side (AC1, AC2, AC5) cannot be covered by a repository test: `rebar-dev-update.sh` is
machine-local and git-ignored, so it lies outside any test's reach. Those are proven by the
observations named in their acceptance criteria, run against the live updater, and the
AC2 resolver is exercised against a harness carrying the real pin.

## Constraints

- Do not pin a local update tool. The required uv version moves as `main` moves, so it must
  be read per candidate commit rather than baked into this host.
- The pin cannot be widened: `check_uv_pin.py` fails the build when `required-version` is
  loosened to a range or overridden per call site, because an exact pin is the property
  under test.
